svg.title: Radiation uses & nuclear energy
svg.desc: Exposure routes: Irradiation: source exposes object; remove/shield source → exposure ends. Contamination: unwanted radioactive material remains and decays. Alpha is especially harmful internally; gamma can irradiate from outside. Dose & precautions: Reduce time, increase distance, use suitable shielding and prevent inhaling/swallowing material. Background: rocks/radon, cosmic rays, living things; fallout adds human-made sources. Location/work affect dose. 1 Sv = 1,000 mSv. Useful emissions: Gamma tracer escapes body; choose half-life long enough to measure, short enough to limit dose. Target radiation to destroy unwanted tissue while limiting healthy-tissue damage. Beta can monitor thin-sheet thickness; gamma sterilises equipment. Judge risks: Same nuclei count: shorter half-life → greater initial activity, faster decline. Long-lived contamination persists. Consider type, dose, position and time with benefit and alternatives. Peer review checks research claims. Fission: Large unstable nucleus usually absorbs a neutron and splits into two smaller nuclei. Releases 2–3 neutrons, gamma and energy; products have kinetic energy. Neutrons can trigger more fissions; reactor controls the chain. Fusion: Two light nuclei join into a heavier nucleus; some mass becomes radiation energy. High temperatures help overcome repulsion; powers stars. Not the same as melting. Both fission and fusion change nuclei.
